cues.o1|Second-order Taylor model: Value, slope, half curvature: terms in 1, p, p². The ½ is the 1/2! of the scalar Taylor series.
cues.o1|First-order necessary condition: Flat ground at the bottom: the tangent plane is horizontal, so the gradient is zero.
cues.o1|Second-order conditions: Necessary: the bowl curves up or stays flat (⪰). Sufficient: zero slope and a bowl curving strictly up (≻).
cues.o1|Quadratic gradient and minimizer: ½xᵀHx differentiates to Hx, bᵀx to b. Scalar check: ½hx² + bx has minimizer −b/h, so x* = −H⁻¹b.
cues.o1|Eigenvalue classification: Curvature along each eigenvector equals its λ: all up is a bowl, all down a dome, mixed a saddle.
cues.o1|Two-variable test: D = det H = λ₁λ₂: positive means equal signs and f_xx picks which; negative means opposite signs, a saddle.
cues.o2|Descent step: Step a distance α along p; downhill requires p at an obtuse angle to ∇f.
cues.o2|Sufficient decrease (Armijo): A shallowed tangent line from f(x) with slope c₁∇fᵀp; accept points on or below it.
cues.o2|Curvature condition: The new slope is at least c₂ times the old negative slope: the slope has flattened, so the step went far enough.
cues.o2|Strong Wolfe condition: Absolute values pinch the slope toward zero from both sides: the point sits near the floor of φ(α).
cues.o2|Exact step on a quadratic: Set φ'(α) = 0: minus slope over curvature along p. Steepest descent gives gᵀg over gᵀAg.
cues.o2|Steepest descent rate: κ = 1 gives ratio 0, one step on circles; large κ gives a ratio near 1, a slow zigzag.
cues.o3|Newton step: Set the model gradient g + Hp to zero: Hessian times step equals minus gradient. One step solves a quadratic exactly.
cues.o3|Quadratic convergence: The error squares each step: 10⁻², 10⁻⁴, 10⁻⁸. Correct digits double.
cues.o3|Secant condition: The matrix maps the step to the gradient change, as f'' ≈ Δf'/Δx in one dimension: Bs = y.
cues.o3|BFGS update: Remove old curvature along s (BssᵀB over sᵀBs), add new curvature yyᵀ over yᵀs. Two rank-one pieces.
cues.o3|Inverse BFGS update: Sandwich H between (I − ρsyᵀ) and (I − ρysᵀ), then add ρssᵀ. Check: H₊y = s.
cues.o3|Linear CG iteration: Step length rᵀr over pᵀAp; the residual updates with Ap; β is new residual squared over old residual squared.
cues.o4|Trust-region subproblem: The same quadratic model as Newton, fenced inside a ball of radius Δ.
cues.o4|Agreement ratio: Actual over predicted: what f delivered over what the model promised.
cues.o4|Radius update rule: Below a quarter, shrink to a quarter. Above three quarters at the boundary, double up to Δ_max.
cues.o4|Exact solution conditions: A Newton system shifted by λI; λ is positive only when the step touches the boundary (complementarity).
cues.o4|Cauchy point: Steepest descent clipped at Δ; with positive curvature along g, τ = ‖g‖³/(Δ gᵀBg) stops at the 1D model minimizer, capped at 1.
cues.o4|Dogleg path: Two straight legs: origin to p_U (steepest descent minimizer), then p_U to p_B (Newton); τ runs from 0 to 2.
cues.o5|Lagrangian: Objective plus a multiplier on each constraint: λ for equalities, μ for inequalities, all added with plus signs.
cues.o5|KKT stationarity: The x-gradient of L is zero: ∇f balanced by the multiplier-weighted constraint gradients.
cues.o5|Feasibility, dual sign, complementari: Feasible point, nonnegative wall forces, and each product μᵢgᵢ = 0: either the wall is touched or its force is zero.
cues.o5|Multiplier sensitivity: Loosen the wall by dc and the optimum drops by μ dc: df* = −μ dc.
cues.o5|Second-order sufficient condition: The Lagrangian curves upward along every direction that slides along the active constraints.
cues.o5|Equality QP KKT system: Symmetric saddle block: Q and Aᵀ on top, A and 0 below; right side −c over b.
cues.o6|Quadratic penalty: Squared violation times μ/2: equalities always count, inequalities count once g crosses zero.
cues.o6|Log barrier: −ln(−g) rises to +∞ as g → 0⁻; the weight μ shrinks toward zero so iterates can approach the wall.
cues.o6|Augmented Lagrangian: Lagrangian plus quadratic penalty; update λ by adding μh, matching the penalty multiplier estimate.
cues.o6|Exact ℓ1 penalty: Absolute violations make a sharp corner at the boundary; ρ larger than the biggest multiplier makes the minimizer exact.
cues.o6|SQP subproblem: Quadratic model of the Lagrangian with linear models of the constraints: Newton's method dressed as a QP.
cues.o6|SQP Newton-KKT system: The equality QP saddle block with Q replaced by ∇²ₓₓL; right side −∇f over −h.
cues.o7|Quadratic response surface: Constant, linears, squares and cross terms: (k + 1)(k + 2)/2 coefficients, 6 for k = 2.
cues.o7|Least squares normal equations: Multiply Φw = y by Φᵀ: the residual is orthogonal to every column of Φ.
cues.o7|Ridge regularization: The normal equations with λ added down the diagonal; λ → 0 recovers least squares.
cues.o7|Radial basis function interpolant: One bump per sample; weights from Ψw = y, so ŷ passes through every data point.
cues.o7|Coefficient of determination: One minus unexplained over total variation: a perfect fit gives 1, the mean alone gives 0.
cues.o7|Expected improvement: Exploit term (f_min − ŷ)Φ(z) rewards a low prediction; explore term sφ(z) rewards uncertainty.
cues.o8|Convex function definition: The chord lies on or above the graph: the weighted average of values is at least the value at the weighted average.
cues.o8|First-order convexity: Every tangent plane lies on or below the graph, everywhere.
cues.o8|Second-order convexity: Curvature is upward or flat in every direction at every point.
cues.o8|Finite differences: Forward is one-sided, O(h). Central is symmetric, the even terms cancel, O(h²), and the denominator spans 2h.
cues.o8|Complex step: Im f(x + ih) = h f'(x) + O(h³): the derivative sits alone in the imaginary part, so tiny h is safe.
cues.o8|Adjoint method: Transposed Jacobian solve with ∂f/∂u on the right; one solve per output, independent of the number of design variables.
cues.o9|Pareto dominance: At least as good in every objective, strictly better in one.
cues.o9|Weighted sum: Normalize each objective from utopia (0) to nadir (1), then blend with weights summing to 1.
cues.o9|ε-constraint method: Keep one objective, fence the others with bounds ε, and sweep the bounds.
cues.o9|Particle swarm update: Inertia, plus a pull toward my best, plus a pull toward the swarm best; random r's add exploration.
cues.o9|Simulated annealing acceptance: Downhill always accepted; uphill accepted with Boltzmann probability exp(−Δf/T), shrinking as T cools.
cues.o9|Nelder-Mead reflection: Reflect the worst point through the centroid of the rest; α = 2 stretches further, ±½ pulls in.
cues.o10|MDF architecture: Converge the full MDA first, then optimize: y is a function of x.
cues.o10|IDF architecture: Coupling guesses become variables; equality constraints make each guess equal its discipline's output.
cues.o10|Coupled Newton solve: Block Jacobian times update equals minus residuals; diagonal blocks are disciplines, off-diagonal blocks are coupling.
cues.o10|Factorial run counts: Levels to the power of factors; each generator halves the two-level run count.
cues.o10|Central composite design: Corners 2ᵏ, two star points per axis 2k, plus centres; rotatable α is the fourth root of the corner count.
cues.o10|Main effect: Average response at high minus average response at low.
